title: Urological Supply Program: Shipment Quantities, Line Periods and Allowed Amounts
content:
Every catheter and accessory line shipped under the Urological Supply Program is governed by the following standard, which also applies to lines the payer denies.

## 1. Monthly quantities

Monthly quantities follow the program: the program's catheters per month (plus its extra catheters with documentation when obstruction, infection or leakage is documented, and never more than one catheter per ordered catheterization per day where the program carries the per-catheterization cap), its lubricant units, insertion trays, bedside bags, leg bags and adhesive remover units per month, measured on the program's supply period basis (rolling from the last service date). Catheters are billed under the program's catheter code and lubricant under the program's lubricant code.

## 2. Line period

One line may cover at most the program's months per shipment. The covers-through date of a line is the day before the same day of the month that many months after the ship date.

*Hypothetical example:* a line covering 3 months that ships on 10 March has a covers-through date of 9 June (the same day of the month three months later is 10 June; the day before it is 9 June).

## 3. Earliest ship date

An item ships no earlier than the program's no-earlier days before the current supply of the item runs out, counting back calendar days from the item's covered-through date with the boundary day included.

- **The item's covered-through date** is the latest covers-through date among the shipped lines of the enrollment for that item code, leaving out any line a recoupment has taken back, up to the handling date. It is empty when the item never shipped on the enrollment.
- **The comparison** is not-earlier-than: a ship date on the boundary day qualifies.
- **The evidence** is the shipment record of this enrollment for this item code.

*Hypothetical boundary cases* (no-earlier figure of 10 calendar days, item covered through 9 June): counting back 10 calendar days from 9 June reaches 30 May. A ship date of 30 May qualifies; a ship date of 29 May does not. If the 9 June line had been taken back by a recoupment and the next latest line of the item were covered through 9 March, the earliest ship date would be counted from 9 March instead.

## 4. Months not shipped

Unshipped months are never added later unless the program allows missed-cycle backfill.

## 5. Allowed amount

The allowed amount of a line is the quantity multiplied by the item's fee (the program's fee per catheter, lubricant fee per unit, insertion tray fee, bedside bag fee, leg bag fee or adhesive remover fee), multiplied by the coverage class's allowed percentage of the fee schedule (a figure of the patient's coverage class under Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility) divided by 100, rounded to the cent half up.

*Hypothetical worked figures* (coverage class percentages chosen for illustration only):

| Line | Quantity and fee | Class percentage | Unrounded | Allowed amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Straight catheters A4351 | 200 at 1.98 USD, that is 396.00 USD | 90 | 356.400 | 356.40 |
| Bedside bag A4357 | 1 at 11.48 USD | 85 | 9.758 | 9.76 |
| Lubricant A4332 | 50 at 0.13 USD, that is 6.50 USD | 85 | 5.525 | 5.53 (half rounds up) |

## 6. Status and setting

Items ship only while the enrollment is active; the evidence is the enrollment's status on the system record. Supplies for a covered skilled nursing stay are not billed where the program excludes covered skilled nursing stays from Summit Ridge billing.

| Enrollment status | Status condition for shipping |
|---|---|
| active | met |
| enrolled-pending | not met; nothing ships |
| on hold | not met; nothing ships |
| cancelled | not met; nothing ships |
